questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial for me that I went to an english speaking country and that I could explore new cultures.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival I felt that the information I needed was easy to find, but I definitely had some troubles with finding information before going.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had some introduction days online on Zoom, which worked out fine. It was basically all the information we got from a letter before arriving, but it was good to get it repeated and have the chance to ask questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Every exchange student had to stay on campus, but thats what you want anyway because with "on campus housing" you will meet other students. 
There are apartments and residence halls/dorm rooms you can stay at on campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You can choose from a variety of different meal plans depending on how much you eat at the on campus options. In my residence hall we had a kitchen in the basement, which I choose to use instead of paying a lot of money for a meal plan. The meal plan is a good option if you want it to be easy, then you dont have to cook or grocery shop.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: All first year students at the university has to live on campus, which means that the residence halls are mostly filled up with 18 year olds freshmens. The apartment complexes are more diverse in age.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's a bit time demanding process. You have to be a bit fast to apply for the classes you want, but it will take some time to get the syllabus from the prof. You need the syllabus so you can get the classes approved at KU. It's a bit confusing, but once you're at the university you have advisors which can help you a lot. There are always a lot of students who drop classes, so even if you didn't get the class you wanted before going then it might come available after.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Faculty advisors

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got everything I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at what earlier exchange students from KU have taken, cause it gives you an idea of whats available to you and which classes are good.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had mostly classes on 300-400 level. It's easier than at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It's smaller classes. Maybe it reminds a bit more of gymnasium classes. 
You may have attendance in some classes, which is very different from KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Labor Economics - EC 431
Game Theory - EC 468
A closer look at capitalism - EC 305
Ressource and environmental economics - EC/ARE 336

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Game theory, because as an economics major you can get it approved as Micro 3.

How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything that you could think of

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I played on the club soccer team, which was so good. It's a great way to meet new people and socialize.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think the most challenging thing is that they drive everywhere and almost everyone has a car. This means that their public transportation system is so bad.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Sports- lots of sports events

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join a club 
If you want to meet other exchange students, then stay at Alexander hall
Go to the sport events, its a huge part of the american culture

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You dont have to buy the meal plan. You can cook yourself.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing a different culture and meeting new people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
